thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: High error rate observed for ILB -> logging-forwarder proxy (503s). Affects Private VPC cross-region traffic; customers reporting delayed responses. Pager triggered for oncall rotation.

mike_h: getting paged in, looking now. seeing tcp retransmit spikes on ILB backend healthchecks.

sara_k: grabbing handoff in 5. mike, paste the top logs you see.

mike_h: putting the essential bits: ```
ILB: backend/10.128.4.23/healthcheck: timeout 120s, status=UNHEALTHY
proxy-forwarder: upstream=logs.vendor.example.com code=503 body="rate_limited" latency=1500ms
netstat: many CLOSE_WAIT to 10.128.4.23:9200
```

ashley_ops: paging customers with privatevpc that hit routing fallback? yes, customer-facing console shows increased tail latency in eu-west1 -> us-east1 failover.

eng-sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2043. Severity: Sev2. Impact: some privatevpc tenants experiencing delayed inference logs and slower request latencies due to ILB backend churn.

julia_r: tl;dr: logging-forwarder (third-party) is throttling egress from our ILB backends -> healthchecks failing -> control plane reroutes cross-region -> clients see higher latency and some 5xx.

mike_h: quick mitigation idea: mark logging-forwarder backend as draining for healthchecks so control plane doesn't use it for user-facing traffic. can do via gcloud or console.

sara_k: we should avoid a full drain if that breaks log delivery; prefer temporary route adjustment. steps: 1) increase backend healthcheck thresholds to be lenient for 10m 2) add traffic policy to prefer same-region backends 3) open emergency bypass to vendor (if available).

mike_h: trying command: ```
gcloud compute backend-services update my-ilb-backend --global --health-checks=hc-lenient-120s
```

eng-sre-bot: Note: changing healthcheck thresholds may delay true failure detection. Approve? :warning:

ashley_ops: approve, short window. Need to notify customers if this persists >30m.

mike_h: change applied. healthcheck interval from 10s->30s, unhealthy threshold 3->6. monitoring dashboards now showing fewer immediate failovers.

julia_r: meanwhile we should confirm vendor side. I opened a support case with logs vendor: SR-7890. They acknowledge backpressure on their ingest frontends and are throttling repeated connections from our aggregator pool.

sara_k: any quick workaround from vendor?

julia_r: vendor suggests retry-backoff tuning and connection pooling reduction to avoid hot-spotting a few upstream pods. also offered a regional ingress endpoint to reduce cross-region hops.

mike_h: actionable: 1) apply lenient healthchecks (done) 2) reduce max connections to vendor on aggregator config to spread across more upstream connections 3) deploy config bump to forwarder replicas to fall back to regional endpoint for eu traffic.

ashley_ops: can we do a fast feature flag to stop forwarding non-essential logs for privatevpc customers as a last resort? customers would prefer latency over logs.

sara_k: yes, feature flag exists: `FORWARDER_DROP_NONCRITICAL` in k8s config. Will flip if vendor workaround fails in 10m.

mike_h: starting a canary rollout for forwarder config with reduced conn pool and regional endpoint routing: ```yaml
# canary snippet
replicas: 3 -> 6
env:
  VENDOR_ENDPOINT: eu-logs-regional.vendor.example.com
  MAX_CONN_PER_WORKER: "50"
```

eng-sre-bot: Deploy started by mike_h at 2043227830. Canary in eu-west1. Watch: cpu, conn, 503 rate.

mike_h: canary shows 70% reduction in 503s to vendor for those pods, and ILB backend health is stable. rolling to remaining replicas.

julia_r: vendor confirms they removed some enforcement rules for our SR and will monitor for 15m. they recommend we spread requests across more IPs to avoid per-IP rate limit.

ashley_ops: customer comms: drafted message to impacted customers explaining degraded log delivery and mitigation steps; offering option to disable noncritical logs for 1 hour. ack?

sara_k: send. include pointer to status page and ETA 30-60m.

mike_h: rolling complete at 2043227988. ILB backend health normalized, control plane stopped cross-region failovers. tail latencies returning to baseline.

eng-sre-bot: Update: Severity reduced to Sev3 at 2043228000. Continue monitoring for 1h.

julia_r: follow-up actions (post-incident): 1) add per-vendor regional endpoint routing in default forwarder config, 2) increase aggregator pool IP diversity (NAT pools), 3) add synthetic probe that simulates vendor throttling to catch regression.

sara_k: logging ticket created: LOG-2043 with remediation checklist and owners assigned to julia_r and mike_h.

ashley_ops: customer messages sent at 2043228015. One customer asked for SLA credit — escalating to support.

mike_h: oncall handoff to sara_k at 2043228030. leaving notes in the incident doc.

sara_k: taking over monitoring. if we see vendor re-throttle, flip `FORWARDER_DROP_NONCRITICAL` to `true`.

eng-sre-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation at 2043228045; postmortem scheduled.

mike_h: final note: this was a third-party throttling event that manifested as ILB backend health churn and caused cross-region routing. important lesson: observability and control-plane interactions can amplify each other.

sara_k: agreed — add routing policy guardrails so vendor-side behavior doesn't trigger control-plane failovers in future.

ashley_ops: thanks team. :thumbsup:
